reasoning: The trap is real, but no attacker can reach it. ZAIWireTypes.swift:83-84 calls Int(Double) with no range check, and AppConfig.swift:199-203 accepts any JSON Double, so a value like 1e19 would abort the process. The problem is the source. It is the response from a hardcoded HTTPS endpoint (ZAIProvider.swift:10, `https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`), which the user cannot configure: there is no base_url knob, unlike Kimi. So the only parties who can shape that JSON are (a) Z.AI itself, the first-party vendor the user already trusts with their API key, or (b) someone who breaks TLS, which gives far more than a crash. The other path, poisoning the DiskCache, needs write access as the same local user under the 0700 Application Support directory, which is already full compromise. The finding admits this by listing 'attacker controls or influences the Z.AI API response' as an assumed precondition, not a demonstrated one. No attacker-controlled source reaches the sink in the default deployment. This is a robustness bug (a vendor schema quirk crashes the app, and the cached payload makes it crash again), not an exploitable vulnerability. Fixing it with Int(exactly:) is still worthwhile as hardening.
